summary: Coronado NF 14x14 ft L-4 groundhouse built 1930-33 on Atascosa Mountain, AZ; NRHP 1988, NHLR 1996; destroyed by the Murphy Fire in June 2011.

facts.design: L-4 type wooden groundhouse, 14 by 14 feet, modified hip roof with 2-foot overhang
facts.status_note: Destroyed in June 2011: NHLR and KOLD name the Murphy Fire; Wikipedia gives June 6 without naming the fire; a Forest Lookouts page gives June 5 and says the lookout and outhouse were destroyed. No source describes the stone cistern or the site now.

visit.trail_note: A 1989 survey said the lookout was accessible by trail only. No source describes access to the site now.

corrections.why: No source gives a height. 3.7 m equals 12 feet, the size a 1967 newspaper item gives for the lookout as a 12 by 12 foot lookout (floor size, not height). NHLR, Wikipedia and the 1989 survey give 14 by 14 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Wikipedia say June 6, 2011; the westlookouts page says June 5, 2011. The story uses June 6 and notes the other date.
NHLR and Wikipedia say 1930 to 1933; the 1989 survey says 1930 or 1933. The brief's 1930 is the earliest of these.
The 1967 newspaper item quoted on westlookouts says 12 by 12 feet; NHLR, Wikipedia and the 1989 survey say 14 by 14 feet. The story uses 14 by 14 and mentions the 1967 figure as the newspaper's.
NHLR gives 6,070 ft (1,850 m); Wikipedia gives 6,235 ft (1,900 m). The brief keeps NHLR's figure. Elevation is not in the story.
Wikipedia and the NRIS record date the listing to 1988, but the 1989 survey recommends the house for National Register eligibility. The story uses 1988.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 3.7 is removed (see corrections). NHLR spells the lookout 'Atacosa' in its fire sentence; kept verbatim in the quote. The KOLD URL spelling ('hiostoric') is as published. The Arizona Daily Star fire story was not read (HTTP 429), so its 6,249 ft elevation is not used. Read budget exceeded (about 9 page reads, mostly to check the destruction date and size); 1 WebSearch used. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story previously said no source mentioned the outhouse after the fire, but the Forest Lookouts page says the lookout and outhouse were destroyed; it now says so. Wikipedia does not name the Murphy Fire, so the story attributes the fire name to NHLR and gives Wikipedia only the date.
